To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) GALR1 mRNA is not co-expressed with cholinergic markers in the medial septal and diagonal band regions; (2) GALR1 is co-expressed with VP and GAL in the BNST and medial amygdaloid regions.
GALR1 mRNA is co-ex-pressed by galanergic neurons in the basal forebrain but is not co-expressed by cholinergic neurons.
(1) GALR1 mRNA is co-ex-pressed by extrahypothamic VP/GAL, but not cholin-ergic neurons, in the BF and (2) the GALR1 mRNA-containing neurons of the BF are likely to be non-cholinergic.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the anatomical and neurochemical basis of memory functions and the role of the neuropeptide galanine and its receptor in the modulation of cholinergic function in the basal forebrain.
understanding the role of GAL in modulating cholinergic transmission, which is thought to be important in learning and memory.
the anatomical and neurochemical organization of the basal forebrain and its projections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GALR1 is co-expressed within extrahypotlamic VP/GAL cells but not BF cholinergic cells.
GALR1 is co-expressed in the majority of extrahypthalamus VP/GAL neurons and that GALR1 may not be co-expressed in BF cholinergic neuron.
GALR1 mRNA is co-expresssed by galanin but not by cholinergic neurons of the rat basal fore brain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GAL may impair cholinergic transmission by indirectly acting via the GALRs expressed in non-cholinergic BF neurons and/or directly acting upon extrahypothamic VP/GAL cells.
GAL, acting through the GALR1 subtype, may impair memory by modulating the activity of non-cholinergic, but not cholin-ergic neurons in the forebrain.

GALR1 receptors are not present in cholinergic neurons and thus GAL does not directly modulate cholinergic function, but GALR1 receptors in non-cholinergic BF neurons could mediate the effects of GAL on BF cholinergic function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GAL receptor subtype GALR1 mRNA is co-expresssed in the majority of extrahypotalamic VP/GAL but not cholinnergic neurons.

the GAL system is not a simple system, and the effects of GAL on memory and other behaviors are likely mediated through the actions of GAL at multiple receptor subtypes and on multiple cell populations.
GALR1 mRNA is expressed in neurons that are not cholinergic and that GAL may act indirectly on cholinergic neurons through these non-cholinergic cells.
